conv.u: When do I use imperfect vs preterite
conv.reply: Preterite vs. imperfect (Pretérito e imperfecto)Spanish has two simple past tenses, and choosing between them is about viewpoint, not about how long something lasted.1. Preterite: completed, bounded events — Use the preterite for an action viewed as finished at a specific point or within a defined period.e.g. Ayer compré un ventilador nuevo. — Yesterday I bought a new fan.2. Preterite: a chain of events — When actions happen one after another and move the story forward, each one is preterite.e.g. Me levanté, me bañé y salí corriendo. — I got up, showered and ran out.3. Preterite: counted times and measured periods — A precise number of repetitions or a period with clear limits makes the action a closed block, so preterite.e.g. Fui al dentista tres veces el mes pasado. — I went to the dentist three times last month.4. Preterite: beginnings, endings and change — Starting, finishing and sudden changes are points in time, so verbs that express them are usually preterite.e.g. La película empezó a las ocho. — The movie started at eight.5. Imperfect: habits and repeated actions — Use the imperfect for what used to happen or would happen regularly, with no count.e.g. De niño, jugaba béisbol todas las tardes. — As a kid, I used to play baseball every afternoon.6. Imperfect: description and background — Use the imperfect to set the scene: time, date, age, weather, appearance, physical and mental states.e.g. Eran las once y hacía un calor terrible. — It was eleven o'clock and it was terribly hot.…6 more in the full guide (Grammar guides › Preterite vs. imperfect).Say quiz me and I’ll quiz you on it, one question at a time.
